title: My girlfriend found the bug in the one screen I did not write myself
author: Mysterious-Bison3735
selftext:
I have been solo on a Godot project for a bit over two years and wrote every line by hand. My day job is backend at a small company and AI is in all of it now, so the game was the one place I kept it out. Not an ethics position or anything. I like writing the gameplay code and I did not want to hand that part off.

The remap screen sat unfinished for most of that. Keyboard rebinding worked, the controller side was a placeholder with the defaults hardcoded in. Conflicts, saving bindings, two input types in the same menu, none of that is interesting to me and it kept sliding down behind things I wanted to build. I develop on keyboard and there is no pad on my desk. The demo went up for Next Fest with it like that.

My girlfriend played it on the Deck. She plays Switch, so she kept hitting the face button on the right to jump, which in my game is dash. About four minutes in she went looking in the menu to swap them and there was nothing in there to click.

I opened glm-5.3, which is what we use at work, and pointed it at that screen and nothing else. It got the input map and the keyboard code that already worked, and that was it. I had the whole thing down as a weekend. It was finished before I went to bed.

On the Deck the labels came out wrong. Left bumper showed as R3, Start showed as L2. No compile error, nothing wrong in the editor, the numbers in the label table are the Godot 3 ones and the engine is 4. The face buttons all read correctly, so I spent most of two hours in the save code before I looked at the table. The fix was a find and replace.

It is the only screen in the game I did not write, and I would have to go back and read the conflict check to tell you how it works. Valve does not ask you to disclose code tools, so there is nothing I have to put on the store page. I have not decided whether I am putting it there anyway.
